summary: Nagios NRPE (5666/tcp) is a MISSING SERVICE MODULE in recce. Port 5666 is absent from svcdetect.PORT_NAMES and serviceenum _PORT/_NAME maps, no signature exists in _SIGNATURES, and no per-service script maps to it. Only Nagios reference in the tree is a generic web-dashboard vuln entry in vuln/vulndb.py:707 (unrelated to NRPE binary protocol). NRPE is a high-value gap: it is an RCE-adjacent daemon (its entire job is to run shell commands on behalf of a remote monitoring server), historically vulnerable to CVE-2013-1362 argument injection when dont_blame_nrpe=1, gated only by an allowed_hosts IP whitelist (no user auth), and its command output leaks logged-in users, mounted filesystems, processes, hostnames, and plugin paths — a rich cross-service seeding surface. NRPE v2 speaks a fixed 1036-byte CRC32-checked packet; v3 added length-prefixed variable payloads; v4 requires TLS (usually anon-DH ADH-AES256-SHA with no cert validation, itself a finding). Build a new recce/services/nrpe.py in the shape of modbus.py (binary probe + findings + runbook + analyze) with ipmi.py-style cred/known_users wiring for enumerated output. Register the port in svcdetect.PORT_NAMES ("nrpe", "Nagios NRPE agent"), add nrpe -> "nrpe" to serviceenum._NAME and 5666 -> "nrpe" to _PORT, and add a byte-signature for the NRPE response header (v2 fixed header 0x00 0x02 0x00 0x02) in _SIGNATURES.

existing_coverage.notes: Only Nagios reference is vulndb.py:707 covering the Nagios XI web dashboard (unauth RCE / default creds against the web UI), NOT the NRPE agent binary protocol on 5666. No probe, no signature, no port map entry, no per-service script mapping. Port 5666 falls through svcdetect (returns unknown) and serviceenum (no script suggestion).

capabilities.name: detect-nrpe-port
capabilities.description: Register 5666/tcp in svcdetect.PORT_NAMES as ('nrpe','Nagios NRPE agent') and in serviceenum _NAME/_PORT so the port stops appearing as unknown and gets a runbook slot. Also add a byte-signature to svcdetect._SIGNATURES matching the NRPE v2 response header (0x00 0x02 0x00 0x02, big-endian: version=2 type=response) so non-standard ports still classify.

capabilities.name: nrpe-version-probe
capabilities.description: Send the built-in _NRPE_CHECK query (packet_type=1/query, command_buffer='_NRPE_CHECK') and parse the response. Reveals NRPE major/minor version (v2 vs v3 vs v4) and confirms this is a live NRPE daemon rather than a random 5666 listener. Version drives which vuln fingerprints apply (CVE-2013-1362 pre-2.15, CVE-2014-2913 pre-2.15, CVE-2020-6581 pre-3.2.1).
capabilities.protocol_reference: NRPE protocol source (nrpe.h) — packet_version=2, packet_type QUERY=1 / RESPONSE=2, buffer[1024]

capabilities.name: nrpe-plaintext-v2-detect
capabilities.description: Attempt an unencrypted v2 handshake first. If the daemon replies in clear (older NRPE builds with use_ssl=0 or plain v2), flag it high — command output, hostnames, and usernames traverse the network in the clear AND anyone reaching the port can invoke commands (no auth in the base protocol). Compare against TLS-only v4 defaults.

capabilities.name: nrpe-anon-dh-tls
capabilities.description: When plaintext fails, retry via TLS with the anonymous-DH cipher suite historically used by NRPE (ADH-AES256-SHA / ADH-AES128-SHA). If the handshake succeeds without a certificate, flag it: anon-DH provides confidentiality but zero server authentication — a MITM can transparently proxy the session, harvest exec output, and forge query packets. This is the default for NRPE 3.x builds and remains common in 4.x.

capabilities.name: nrpe-command-enumeration
capabilities.description: Probe a curated list of default check commands (check_load, check_disk, check_users, check_procs, check_swap, check_total_procs, check_zombie_procs, check_mem, check_cpu, check_uptime, check_hostname, check_mailq, check_ntp_time, check_ide_smart, check_apt, check_yum). Each successful invocation is a live registered command; each 'NRPE: Command not defined' response is negative evidence. Builds the attack surface map for arg-injection targeting and reveals what the monitoring surface actually exposes.

capabilities.name: nrpe-arg-injection-cve-2013-1362
capabilities.description: Send a command that accepts $ARG1$ substitution (any command line in nrpe.cfg with $ARGx$) with metachars in the argument: bang-separator ! then shell metacharacters (;, `, $(...), \n, |). On daemons built with --enable-command-args AND configured with dont_blame_nrpe=1, NRPE substitutes into the shell exec unquoted → arbitrary command execution as the nagios user. Test with a benign payload like 'check_something!\`id\`' or 'a && echo RECCE_MARKER' and search the response for the marker or 'uid=' before declaring RCE.

capabilities.name: nrpe-metachar-bypass-cve-2014-2913
capabilities.description: CVE-2014-2913 patch for CVE-2013-1362 blocked most metachars but missed newline (0x0a) when dont_blame_nrpe=1. Send a payload containing a literal LF to bypass the sanitizer and still get shell exec. Only applies to NRPE 2.15 / early 2.x patched builds.

capabilities.name: nrpe-response-oob-cve-2020-6581
capabilities.description: NRPE < 3.2.1 has an out-of-bounds read in the response parser (length field vs. buffer). Fingerprint by version disclosed from _NRPE_CHECK; do NOT attempt to trigger — this is a client-side crash primitive that mostly matters as a DoS/info-disclosure vector on the monitoring server. Report as version-tagged finding, no exploit sent.

capabilities.name: nrpe-allowed-hosts-inferred-permissive
capabilities.description: NRPE has NO user authentication — allowed_hosts is the entire ACL. If recce's scanner IP reaches the daemon and receives a valid response, the allowed_hosts entry is either wildcarded, contains a broad CIDR, or is unset. Report the source IP that got through as evidence the ACL includes it, and cite that best practice restricts to the Nagios/Icinga server IP(s) only. This is often the finding operators care about most because the ACL is the sole gate on remote command execution.

capabilities.name: nrpe-check-users-user-harvest
capabilities.description: Invoke check_users (or check_procs -a) and parse the response: check_users returns 'USERS OK - N users currently logged in' and, in verbose mode / on some plugins, lists names. check_procs with -f flag can leak process argv including bind addresses, database strings, and connection args. Emit each username seen to feed known_users for reuse against SSH / SMB / LDAP / IPMI / MSSQL. High-signal cheap read.

capabilities.name: nrpe-check-hostname-selfid
capabilities.description: Invoke check_hostname (when present) or parse check_uptime / check_load response for the hostname string plugins often prefix. Emit hostname to known_hostnames so it feeds TLS-SAN checks, Kerberos realm inference, and reverse-lookup validation across other services (LDAP, SMB, MSSQL).

capabilities.name: nrpe-plugin-path-os-fingerprint
capabilities.description: Error paths in check-not-found responses ('/usr/lib/nagios/plugins/check_x not found' vs '/usr/lib64/nagios/plugins/...' vs '/opt/local/libexec/...') fingerprint the OS/distribution (Debian vs RHEL/CentOS vs macports vs FreeBSD). Also confirms whether NRPE is running under a container (paths like /app/nagios). Cheap OS classification with zero extra traffic.

capabilities.name: nrpe-monitored-service-inference
capabilities.description: The set of configured check_ commands implies what else runs on the host: check_mysql → MySQL locally, check_pgsql → PostgreSQL, check_http → local web app, check_smtp → mail, check_dns → resolver, check_oracle_health → Oracle, check_ldap → LDAP. Cross-reference against ports actually seen open on this host by the port sweep — an implied service with no open port is a bound-to-127.0.0.1 target reachable ONLY via the NRPE RCE (a pivot signal for the operator).

capabilities.name: nrpe-crc32-integrity-only
capabilities.description: The NRPE v2 packet CRC32 is integrity-only, not a MAC — anyone who can reach the socket can craft valid packets. Note this once alongside plaintext-v2 detection to explain why plaintext + no-auth means anyone on-path can invoke any registered command. Documentation-grade finding that sharpens the plaintext one.

capabilities.name: nrpe-tls-cert-harvest
capabilities.description: When NRPE v4 is deployed with a real certificate (not anon-DH), extract the server cert CN and SANs during the TLS handshake. Feed to known_hostnames for cross-service validation. Also record the cert fingerprint so a fleet-wide scan clusters agents that share the same cert (common when one image is redeployed).

cross_service_wire_candidates: known_users: parse check_users (logged-in user names) and check_procs -f (process owner column, argv strings) — seeds SSH/SMB/LDAP/IPMI/MSSQL/PostgreSQL/MySQL password-spray and cred re-use

known_hostnames: parse check_hostname output, check_load/check_uptime hostname prefix, and NRPE v4 TLS cert CN/SAN — seeds Kerberos realm inference, TLS SAN validation, LDAP base-DN guessing, reverse-DNS cross-check
known_domains: extract FQDN suffix from hostname / TLS SAN — seeds Kerberos/AD/LDAP realm discovery

implied_local_services (NEW shared surface): the set of configured check_ commands (check_mysql / check_pgsql / check_oracle_health / check_http / check_ldap / check_smtp / check_dns / check_ntp_time / check_mailq) implies services listening on 127.0.0.1 that the port sweep can't see — a NEW cross-service surface that pivot planning, RCE-payload staging, and lateral-movement suggestions should read from

os_fingerprint: plugin path prefix (/usr/lib vs /usr/lib64 vs /opt/local) refines host OS beyond nmap OS guess — consumed by exploit selection, package-version heuristics, path assumptions in other modules

rce_footholds (NEW shared surface): if CVE-2013-1362 arg-injection succeeds, this host becomes a confirmed code-exec pivot as user 'nagios' — feed to a shared 'rce_footholds' registry that session/persistence/pivot planners read for staging targets

monitoring_server_candidates (NEW shared surface): allowed_hosts is the whitelist of Nagios/Icinga monitoring server IPs; if we later gain code-exec, /etc/nagios/nrpe.cfg reads that list — those IPs are high-value follow-on scan targets (the monitoring server itself typically has SSH keys or agent trust into every monitored host)
relay_targets: a monitoring host reached from NRPE config → likely SSH/WinRM/agent trust outward to every host it monitors (feed relay_targets style pivot list)

cred_material_paths: post-RCE, ~nagios/.ssh/, /etc/nagios/resource.cfg (contains $USER1$..$USERN$ macros often holding DB passwords for check_mysql / check_pgsql / check_oracle) → feed known_hashes / known_credentials
tls_cert_registry: NRPE v4 cert fingerprint clusters identically-provisioned hosts across the fleet — useful for the (planned) cert-fingerprint cross-service map
implementation_notes: Create recce/services/nrpe.py in the shape of recce/services/modbus.py (line 1-243): module docstring explaining protocol + findings; _DEFAULT_PORT=5666, _TIMEOUT=4.0; is_nrpe(port) predicate matching portid==5666 or 'nrpe' in service/product; a _build_v2_query(command, args) that packs the fixed 1036-byte NRPE v2 packet (2B version=2, 2B type=1/query, 4B CRC32=0 placeholder, 2B result_code=0, 1024B buffer command\\x00pad\\xff+2B pad, then recompute CRC32 over the whole thing and patch bytes 4-7); a _build_v3_query() for length-prefixed variant; _parse_response(data) that reads the response type=2 packet and returns (result_code, buffer_text); a probe() that first tries plaintext v2 _NRPE_CHECK, falls back to TLS with ctx.set_ciphers('ALL:@SECLEVEL=0:ADH-AES256-SHA:ADH-AES128-SHA') and ctx.check_hostname=False; a nrpe_targets(hosts) collector; _finding() helper matching modbus.py line 159; findings(hosts, probes) that emits the enumerated finding list; runbook(ip, port) with check_nrpe -H host -p 5666 -c _NRPE_CHECK and -c check_users lines; findings_to_vulns delegating to svccommon; analyze(hosts, creds, active, budget, progress) matching the modbus.py signature at line 221 for scheduler compat. For the cred/known_users wiring, mirror ipmi.py line 604-621 (from ..creds.known_users import known_users; picked = known_users(hosts, cap=17, extras=[...])) if we ever want to pre-seed users to test with check_procs -u <user>. Register port in svcdetect.PORT_NAMES: 5666: ('nrpe','Nagios NRPE agent'). Add signature in _SIGNATURES: (re.compile(r'^\\x00\\x02\\x00\\x02'), 'nrpe','Nagios NRPE'). Add to serviceenum._NAME: 'nrpe':'nrpe' and _PORT: 5666:'nrpe'. Create recce/scripts/recce-service-nrpe.sh runbook alongside. Add a vulndb entry for CVE-2013-1362 keyed on the nrpe_arg_injection_rce finding kind. Airgap-safe: stdlib socket + ssl + struct + zlib.crc32 only; no external tools required at scan time (check_nrpe / nagios-nrpe-plugin is referenced only in the runbook for the operator).
